\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قبض} (qabaḍa)}{قبض (qabaḍa)}]{\ar{قبض} (qabaḍa) — to seize, to grasp}

\label{lesson:AR-C317-qabada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for rubble, then the Arabic for ruins.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قبض}}
\textbf{\ar{قبض}} — \emph{qabaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to seize, to grasp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قبضت} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{على} \ar{اللص} \ar{في} \ar{السوق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qabaḍat ash-shurṭa ʿalā al-liṣṣ fī as-sūq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police caught the thief in the market.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقبض}, \emph{yaqbiḍ}.

\ar{قبض} \ar{على}: to arrest. \ar{قبض} \ar{راتبه}: he drew his pay.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قبض}} (\emph{qabaḍa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-b-ḍ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to take a thing in the closed hand\textquotedblright{}; \emph{qabḍa} is a fist.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qabaḍa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qabaḍa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qabaḍat ash-shurṭa ʿalā al-liṣṣ fī as-sūq.} — The police caught the thief in the market.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for rubble, then the Arabic for ruins, then say \emph{qabaḍa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{قبض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To seize, to grasp\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{احتجز} (iḥtajaza)}{احتجز (iḥtajaza)}]{\ar{احتجز} (iḥtajaza) — to detain, to hold}

\label{lesson:AR-C317-ihtajaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for ruins, then the Arabic for to seize.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{احتجز}}
\textbf{\ar{احتجز}} — \emph{iḥtajaza} — \textquotedblleft{}to detain, to hold\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{احتجز} \ar{الموظف} \ar{جواز} \ar{سفري} \ar{ساعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iḥtajaza al-muwaẓẓaf jawāz safarī sāʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The official held my passport for an hour.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحتجز}, \emph{yaḥtajiz}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{احتجز}} (\emph{iḥtajaza}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-j-z} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to keep apart, to hold back\textquotedblright{}. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to hold back for oneself\textquotedblright{}; a hotel booking, \emph{ḥajz}, is the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtajaza}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtajaza}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iḥtajaza al-muwaẓẓaf jawāz safarī sāʿa.} — The official held my passport for an hour.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for ruins, then the Arabic for to seize, then say \emph{iḥtajaza} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{احتجز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To detain, to hold\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أوقف} (awqafa)}{أوقف (awqafa)}]{\ar{أوقف} (awqafa) — to stop someone; to arrest}

\label{lesson:AR-C317-awqafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to seize, then the Arabic for to detain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أوقف}}
\textbf{\ar{أوقف}} — \emph{awqafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to stop someone; to arrest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أوقف} \ar{الشرطي} \ar{السيارة} \ar{عند} \ar{الجسر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{awqafa ash-shurṭī as-sayyāra ʿinda al-jisr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The policeman stopped the car at the bridge.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يوقف}, \emph{yūqif}.

\ar{توقف} is to stop oneself; \ar{أوقف} is to stop someone or something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أوقف}} (\emph{awqafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-q-f} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to stand still\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{tawaqqafa}, to stop. It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to make stand still\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{awqafa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{awqafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{awqafa ash-shurṭī as-sayyāra ʿinda al-jisr.} — The policeman stopped the car at the bridge.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to seize, then the Arabic for to detain, then say \emph{awqafa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أوقف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To stop someone; to arrest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{دورية} (dawriyya)}{دورية (dawriyya)}]{\ar{دورية} (dawriyya) — a patrol}

\label{lesson:AR-C317-dawriyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to detain, then the Arabic for to stop someone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{دورية}}
\textbf{\ar{دورية}} — \emph{dawriyya} — \textquotedblleft{}a patrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مرت} \ar{دورية} \ar{شرطة} \ar{في} \ar{الشارع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{marrat dawriyyat shurṭa fī ash-shāriʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A police patrol went by in the street.
\end{quote}

Also a periodical: \ar{مجلة} \ar{دورية}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{دورية}} (\emph{dawriyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-w-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to turn, to go round\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{dawr}, a turn. A \emph{dawriyya} makes its round again and again.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dawriyya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dawriyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marrat dawriyyat shurṭa fī ash-shāriʿ.} — A police patrol went by in the street.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to detain, then the Arabic for to stop someone, then say \emph{dawriyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{دورية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A patrol\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حاجز} (ḥājiz)}{حاجز (ḥājiz)}]{\ar{حاجز} (ḥājiz) — a checkpoint; a barrier}

\label{lesson:AR-C317-hajiz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to stop someone, then the Arabic for a patrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حاجز}}
\textbf{\ar{حاجز}} — \emph{ḥājiz} — \textquotedblleft{}a checkpoint; a barrier\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وقفت} \ar{السيارات} \ar{عند} \ar{الحاجز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waqafat as-sayyārāt ʿinda al-ḥājiz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cars stopped at the checkpoint.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{حواجز}, \emph{ḥawājiz}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حاجز}} (\emph{ḥājiz}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-j-z} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to keep two things apart\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Ḥājiz} is the participle: \textquotedblleft{}what stands between\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥājiz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥājiz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waqafat as-sayyārāt ʿinda al-ḥājiz.} — The cars stopped at the checkpoint.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to stop someone, then the Arabic for a patrol, then say \emph{ḥājiz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حاجز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A checkpoint; a barrier\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
